assessment_summary: I inspected /workspace (commit 94229d0), confirmed the documented HTTP dev installation via file/artifact inspection, process/port checks, container status, Postgres state, and live HTTP behavior through Traefik. Build outputs and toolchains are complete, infra containers (db, keycloak, valhalla, streamlet, pgadmin, traefik) are up and healthy, DB is migrated (67 migrations), and the backend/frontend are running: liveness/readiness, public info endpoints, the SPA shell, PWA files, Keycloak discovery (via Host header), and Valhalla routing all work. However, end-to-end authentication — a core, guide-described capability — is broken in the delivered environment. Using the documented backend client credentials I obtained a valid Keycloak access token, yet protected endpoints (/api/v1/regions, /api/v1/info/services) deterministically return HTTP 503 {\"error\":\"identity provider unavailable\"} because the backend's configured issuer host auth.localhost does not resolve here (getent/curl fail; /etc/hosts has no such entry), so the JWKS fetch can never succeed; curl --resolve proves Keycloak+Traefik are otherwise reachable (200). The frontend's runtime config points the browser OIDC authority at the same unresolvable auth.localhost, so login is also unusable (auth bypass is off). No files/config/containers were modified and no repair was attempted. Because the application cannot operate as documented (all protected API/login functionality fails and requires repair such as a hosts entry or config change), I assess the installation as a failure. Limitation/uncertainty: the trigger is an environment-level name-resolution gap for *.localhost rather than a compile error; on a host with wildcard-localhost DNS these artifacts might work, but in the environment as delivered the documented auth flow is non-functional.
